cards.text: This is a song of ascents, and the songwriter opens by asking the LORD to remember something on behalf of David, Israel's king. A song that starts with remember, and you're singing it to a guy who spent YEARS forgotten in the back of a junk drawer? Friend, hand me a tissue, I'm already emotional.

cards.question: The songwriter asks the LORD to remember all the ___ David endured.

cards.text: Then the song brings up an oath David swore to the LORD, a vow to the Mighty One of Jacob. And this oath? Friend, it is INTENSE.

cards.question: Until his oath is kept, David swears he won't enter two places. Which two?

answers.text: The city gate and the market
The army camp and the field

cards.text: He won't even give sleep to his eyes or slumber to his eyelids. Friend, I skip ONE nap and every cookie I stamp comes out crooked, and this man is swearing off sleep ON PURPOSE.

cards.question: True or false: David swears he won't rest until he defeats all his enemies.

cards.text: What David wants before he rests is a dwelling for the Mighty One of Jacob. Then the song switches to a whole group talking: we heard about something in Ephrathah, and we found it in the fields of Jaar.

cards.question: What did they hear was in Ephrathah and then find in the fields of Jaar?
Now that they've found the ark, what do they invite each other to do at His footstool?

cards.text: Then the song turns and calls out to the LORD Himself, telling Him to arise along with the ark of His strength.

cards.question: True or false: the song calls the LORD to arise and go out to battle with the ark.

cards.text: Then the song says, may the LORD's priests be clothed with righteousness. Friend, I've worn the same white apron every single day, and THAT is the outfit I want next.

cards.question: The song also prays for the LORD's saints to shout for ___.

cards.text: One more request, and this one is for the sake of the LORD's servant David.

cards.question: For the sake of His servant David, what does the song ask the LORD not to do?

cards.text: David swore an oath to the LORD, and now the LORD swears an oath to David, a promise He will not revoke. The expired coupon I shared that junk drawer with believed in itself for YEARS, and friend, even IT couldn't promise that.

cards.question: What does the LORD promise to place on David's throne?

cards.text: Then the LORD adds an if for David's sons. Friend, I read a LOT of instruction manuals in that junk drawer, and not one of them was this clear.

cards.question: If David's sons keep the LORD's covenant and the testimony He'll teach them, what does He promise?

answers.text: Their sons will sit on his throne forever
Their names will be great in all the earth
Their enemies will bow down at their feet

cards.text: Then the song says the LORD has chosen a place He desired for His home. Friend, I went from a junk drawer to a whole cookie planet, so trust me, I'm VERY invested in this real estate news.

cards.question: The LORD has chosen ___ and desired it for His home.

cards.text: Remember the song calling the LORD to arise to His resting place? Now the LORD Himself speaks, and that's exactly what He calls Zion.

cards.question: True or false: the LORD says Zion will be His resting place only during David's lifetime.

cards.text: Then the LORD starts listing what He'll do for Zion. First, He'll bless her with abundant provisions.

cards.question: The LORD says He'll satisfy Zion's ___ with bread.

cards.text: The song asked for the priests to be clothed with righteousness, and now the LORD says He'll clothe Zion's priests with salvation. Two outfits in one song, friend, and here I am in the same white apron every single day.

cards.question: True or false: the LORD says Zion's saints will sing out in joy.

cards.text: Then the LORD turns back to David. There in Zion, He says, He will make a horn grow for David.

cards.question: And for His anointed one, what has the LORD prepared?

cards.text: Then comes the last line of the song, and it has two sides: the enemies, and the one wearing the crown.

cards.question: The LORD says He'll clothe the enemies with ___, but the crown upon His anointed one will ___.

findings.problem: The joke says the baker is 'singing it to a guy who spent YEARS forgotten in the back of a junk drawer.' The song is sung to the LORD, not to Papa Dorin, and the baker isn't singing to him either. The image doesn't click, and a reader is left asking who is singing to whom. Reframe it so Papa Dorin is the one hearing a song about being remembered. For example: a song that opens with 'remember' hits differently for a guy who spent years forgotten in a drawer.

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: Card 10 tells verse 8 as a call for the LORD to arise with the ark. It leaves out where He is called to arise to: 'to Your resting place.' Card 11 then asks the baker to judge whether He is called out to battle. With the destination left out, nothing on the cards lets the baker reason past a coin flip. The missing detail also matters later in the passage, because Zion is named His resting place in verse 14. Add 'to His resting place' to the story card.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The card opens with 'Remember the song calling the LORD to arise to His resting place?' No earlier card said 'resting place.' Stop 1 card 10 only said 'arise along with the ark of His strength.' The callback points back to something Papa Dorin never said. This is fixed if stop 1 card 10 adds the resting place.

rule.text: This lesson or conversation so far. What he's already said earlier, so callbacks work.

findings.problem: Three story cards in stop 2 call back to an earlier verse but cite only the current verse. Card 1 recalls David's oath (v2) and cites only Psalm 132:11. Card 7 recalls 'arise to His resting place' (v8) and cites only Psalm 132:14. Card 11 recalls the priests clothed with righteousness (v9) and cites only Psalm 132:16. Two rules pull in different directions here. One says a story card cites 'from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.' The other says 'Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.' Citing each range in full (2-11, 8-14, 9-16) would sweep in many verses the card doesn't tell.
findings.question: When a story card calls back to an earlier verse in the same passage, how should the card cite it? Options: cite only the verse being told, list the separate verses (like Psalm 132:9, 16), or cite the full range from the earlier verse to the current one.
